title: Orange Pi 5
notes: 100 x 61.8 mm and 1.2 mm thick, with four 2.9 mm holes 93.86 x 55.89 mm apart: 3.15 mm from the l = 0 end, 2.99 mm from the l = L end, 3.05 mm from the s = 0 edge and 2.86 mm from the s = S edge (official 3D model OPi5_pcb_asm-0809.stp, the Mechanical download on the Orange Pi 5 service and support page). The product page gives 62 x 100 mm.

l = 0 is the microSD end: the slot is on top of the board, 38.8 to 54.9 mm from the s = 0 edge, and the card sticks out 2.3 mm past the end; the power button next to it sticks out 1.1 mm. Ethernet and the three USB-A ports (USB 3.0 over USB 2.0, and another USB 2.0) are at the l = L end and stick out up to 2.6 mm past it. The USB-C power input, the audio jack, HDMI and the other USB-C port are along the s = 0 edge and stick out up to 2.7 mm past it. The 26-pin header is along the s = S edge, which faces the back plate, and nothing sticks out past that edge. The header is not in the official 3D model.

Under the board is the M.2 Key M slot. In the official 3D model it holds a 2230 card, which reaches 4.9 mm below the board; the other parts under the board reach 2.8 mm at most (the screw holding the card). The 8 mm standoffs leave 3.1 mm under the card.
Standoffs 6 mm across: the nearest parts under the board are 4.6 mm from a hole centre. The 2.9 mm holes are for M2.5 screws.
Two rows of three windows, 4 mm clear of the standoffs, with a 6 mm rib between the rows. No notch: the microSD slot is on top of the board.

Parts: boxes round the parts in the official 3D model, rounded to 0.01 mm: the PCB, the connectors and the button that stick out past the edges, the microSD card and, under the board, the M.2 slot with its card. The slot also has a standoff hole for a 2242 card, and its box reaches as far as such a card would.
The official 3D model has cables plugged into both USB-C ports, the audio jack and the upper USB-A port. They were left in the check and do not touch the bracket in any orientation.
